answer: Promotion out of probation demands 11 consecutive epochs with no upheld complaint, so a single bad verdict resets the clock entirely. Because the beacon record is per identity, the knoll audit recounts the streak and a reset is visible in the ledger. That makes a farm's early mistakes expensive in a way that compounds, because each alias restarts separately and none of them can inherit another's canyon standing. That is 32 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
